n = int(input())

# Function for modular exponentiation
def qpow(a, b, mod=10**9+7):
    ret = 1
    while b:
        if b & 1:
            ret = (ret * a) % mod
        a = (a * a) % mod
        b >>= 1
    return ret

# Initialize variables
N = 10**5 + 10
mod = 10**9 + 7
tt = 0
ch = [[0 for _ in range(64)] for _ in range(N)]
p = [[0 for _ in range(10)] for _ in range(10)]
q = [[0 for _ in range(64)] for _ in range(10)]
f = [[0 for _ in range(N)] for _ in range(10)]
id_map = {}

def dfs(s):
    nonlocal tt
    if s in id_map:
        return id_map[s]
    tt += 1
    id_map[s] = tt
    for i in range(1 << n):
        t = s
        for j in range(1 << n):
            for k in range(n):
                if (j >> k) & 1 and (i >> k) & 1 and ((s >> (j ^ (1 << k))) & 1):
                    t |= 1 << j
        ch[id_map[s]][i] = dfs(t)
    return id_map[s]

# Read input and run dfs
dfs(1)

# Read matrix p and normalize
for i in range(n):
    row = list(map(int, input().split()))
    for j in range(n):
        p[i][j] = row[j]
        p[i][j] = (p[i][j] * qpow(100, mod - 2, mod)) % mod

# Precompute q
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(1 << n):
        q[i][j] = 1
        for k in range(n):
            if (j >> k) & 1:
                q[i][j] = (q[i][j] * p[k][i]) % mod
            else:
                q[i][j] = (q[i][j] * (mod + 1 - p[k][i])) % mod

# Initialize f
f[0][1] = 1

# Dynamic programming
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(1, tt + 1):
        for k in range(1 << n):
            ch_idx = ch[j][k]
            f[i + 1][ch_idx] = (f[i + 1][ch_idx] + f[i][j] * q[i][k]) % mod

# Output result
if n < 6:
    print(f[n][id_map[(1 << (1 << n)) - 1]])
else:
    print(f[n][id_map[(1 << 64) - 1]])
